about: Dive sites, fish and rules for the British Virgin Islands. Written from general knowledge and kept simple: sizes and limits here are the game's, not the territory's. In life a visitor may not spearfish or take lobster in the BVI at all; the game lets the skipper do it and says so.

water.say: Warm blue water over coral. 26 degrees: a rash vest will do. In life visitors may not spearfish here; lionfish are the catch everybody is asked to take

lobster.name: Caribbean spiny lobster
lobster.say: Caribbean spiny lobster: under the coral ledges by day, walking the sand at night. By hand only, 89 mm across the carapace, two a day, closed August to October

species.name: lionfish
species.encouraged: An invader from the Pacific that eats the reef's young fish. Every one taken is a favour to the reef
species.say: Lionfish: striped, with a mane of spines, and it does not belong here. The one fish you are asked to take. Mind the spines

species.name: yellowtail snapper
species.say: Yellowtail snapper: a yellow stripe and a forked yellow tail, in mid-water over the reef. 30 cm to keep

species.name: red hind
species.say: Red hind, a small grouper: red spots, sits on the bottom by a hole. 38 cm to keep, two a day, and leave the big ones to breed

species.name: bar jack
species.say: Bar jack: silver and quick, hunting along the edge of the reef in a small pack

species.name: silversides
species.say: A cloud of silversides, turning all at once

species.name: sergeant major
species.say: Sergeant majors: yellow with black bars, everywhere, and too small to bother

species.name: stoplight parrotfish
species.protected: Parrotfish graze the reef clean and make its sand. They are protected and may not be taken
species.say: Parrotfish: green and blue with a beak, biting at the coral. They keep the reef alive and are protected

species.name: southern stingray
species.spare: A stingray is left to the sand
species.say: A southern stingray under a dusting of sand, two eyes showing. It lifts off and glides away if you come too close

species.name: nurse shark
species.spare: A nurse shark asleep under a ledge is left asleep
species.say: A nurse shark, brown and blunt, asleep under a ledge with its head in the dark. Harmless if it is let alone

species.name: green moray
species.say: A green moray, as thick as your arm, head out of a hole in the coral. The gaping is breathing, not a threat

species.name: hawksbill turtle
species.say: A hawksbill turtle, rowing along the reef and stopping to bite at a sponge. Protected. Give it room to come up for air

species.name: great barracuda
species.spare: A barracuda is poor eating here and may carry ciguatera: leave it
species.say: A great barracuda, hanging still and watching you with its teeth showing. It is only curious. Big ones here can carry ciguatera, so nobody eats them

zones.name: Rhone National Marine Park
zones.say: The wreck of the Rhone lies in a national marine park: nothing may be taken, alive or off the wreck

sites.name: The Indians
sites.say: Four rock pinnacles standing out of the sea off Pelican Island, with coral walls, sea fans and a tunnel between them

sites.name: The Caves
sites.say: Three sea caves in the cliff at Treasure Point, said to be where the pirates' silver was found. Shallow, clear and full of fish

sites.name: Wreck of the Rhone
sites.say: The Royal Mail steamer Rhone, lost on Black Rock Point in the hurricane of 1867. Her stern lies in seven metres, her bow in twenty and more
